served.stem: A cytotoxic T cell presses Fas ligand against the Fas receptor on the surface of a target cell, and the target cell dies by apoptosis. Which pathway did that use, and which caspase is switched on first?
choices: The extrinsic pathway, working through a death receptor, activating caspase-8
The extrinsic pathway, working through cytochrome c release, activating caspase-9
Neither pathway, since Fas binding produces necrosis rather than apoptosis
The intrinsic pathway, working through a death receptor, activating caspase-3 first
The intrinsic pathway, working through the mitochondrion, activating caspase-9
served.bankWhy: Sort these by where the signal comes from. A ligand binding a death receptor on the outside of the cell is the extrinsic pathway, and it activates caspase-8 right at the membrane. Trouble arising inside the cell, such as DNA damage that cannot be repaired, is the intrinsic pathway, working through the mitochondrion and caspase-9. Both funnel into the same executioner caspases, so the only thing you have to hold separate is the trigger and the initiator.

answer.text: The extrinsic pathway, working through a death receptor, activating caspase-8
answer.line: The signal came from outside, through Fas, a death receptor. That is the extrinsic pathway, and its first caspase is caspase-8.

steps: Spot where the signal starts. Fas ligand on the T cell binds Fas on the target's surface, so the signal comes from outside: extrinsic.
Fas clusters and pulls in procaspase-8, so caspase-8 is the first caspase switched on.
Caspase-8 then turns on executioners such as caspase-3. Cytochrome c and caspase-9 belong to the inside route, through the mitochondrion.

choices.text: Neither pathway, since Fas binding produces necrosis rather than apoptosis
choices.note: Fas runs a controlled caspase program with every mark of apoptosis. Necrosis is uncontrolled swelling and bursting.

choices.text: The intrinsic pathway, working through a death receptor, activating caspase-3 first
choices.note: A death receptor is right, but that makes it extrinsic. Caspase-3 is an executioner, switched on after the initiator.

choices.text: The intrinsic pathway, working through the mitochondrion, activating caspase-9
choices.note: This describes the intrinsic route, set off by damage inside the cell. This signal came from outside, through a surface receptor.

visual.alt: Two routes into apoptosis. Left, extrinsic: Fas ligand on a T cell binds the Fas death receptor in the membrane, and caspase-8 switches on first, outlined as the answer. Right, intrinsic: damage inside makes the mitochondrion release cytochrome c, and caspase-9 switches on; both routes end at the executioner caspases.
